messages.subject: Debugging strategy: dump your environment.
parts:
I apologize if this has been mentioned before. I don't think I have
seen this one written anywhere so thought I would mention. I believe
this would work on a cluster with copyFiles=TRUE and some thought to
where files are going, though I debug on local so that is where it is
tested.

If you are familiar with debugger() in R you know that R errors arn't
actually R crashing or anything. It is simply an activity that R goes
to when your script is nonsense (by whatever measure). One thing we
can do is tell R to save the environment when it gets to error in your
map/reduce code. Since, the save the environment code is executed
before Rhipe's java gets any shot at the error the rest proceeds as
normal in map/reduce jobs. Also, though we want to save the
environment to a unique file name so that if two mappers error at the
same time there is no nonsense to think about.

It loops like this in my code:

hloess.map = function(map.keys, map.values){
old.error = options("error")
options(error = function() save.image(paste("error.env",
map.keys[[1]],".RData",sep="")))
<doing work>
options(old.error)
}

If some where in <doing work> R chokes on an evaluation it executes a
save of the global environment image and then Rhipe takes over with
the error handling. Now when we return to R we can (and I go to
another R instance for this step). load the error.env.###.RData and
ls() the environment. Eg in R load("error.env0.RData"). Usually it
is map.values *at the time of the error* that I immediately print out.

The value of operating in this way is that its kind of a generic
little piece of code you can cut and paste, and if you error great you
got an image to look at it. If not it does nothing.

Like I said though this is a strategy well suited to local debugging,
and everything from there is a tad more nuanced.

Though it occured to me on the way home that on the cluster I should
worry about dumping the entire contents of a huge dataset into a
series of .RData file dumps.

Which raises the questions:
1) Does Rhipe kill a hadoop job on a map error(or does it have an
option), and failing that,
2) Is it possible to kill a hadoop job from inside a Rhipe map without
knowing the ID of your job (I could add such a thing to the error
function).

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: Debugging strategy: dump your environment.
parts:
On Thu, Mar 3, 2011 at 6:27 PM, Jeremiah Rounds
<roundsj...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Though it occured to me on the way home that on the cluster I should
> worry about dumping the entire contents of a huge dataset into a
> series of .RData file dumps.
>

This is nice. The closest I came to was wrapping stuff
in tryCatch and saving the errors. But your code is cleaner.
(see [1]). be careful loading these saved environments, in case
map.values / map.keys is very large.

> Which raises the questions:
> 1) Does Rhipe kill a hadoop job on a map error(or does it have an
> option), and failing that,

If it's an R error it does indeed kill the job. Also it depends on how
large the input data is. If the data is small and the R error is
thrown after all the data has been read, the job dies only if rhstatus
is monitoring it from the R console (autokill=TRUE). Otherwise it runs
to the end, but the counters will have R_ERRORS in it.

In other cases if an R error is thrown while hadoop is still reading
data then this error is converted to a Java exception and the job
fails. The source can be changed to not throw an exception (the Java
source which converts R errors to Java exceptions).

> 2) Is it possible to kill a hadoop job from inside a Rhipe map without
> knowing the ID of your job (I could add such a thing to the error
> function).

Throw an R error. If you're running rhstatus (from R command line) and
you throw an R error, it will kill the job.

What I don't know (haven't checked) is that if a job dies, will the
files copied to the output.folder (by copyFiles) remain or be removed
by Hadoop.

Regards
J


[1] https://groups.google.com/d/msg/rhipe/x4BO8oOaoBk/9QMEaWdVniAJ>
